about.title: Personal Injury Help in Alameda, California
about.longDescription:
Alameda sits on an island, and most trips on or off it funnel through a handful of streets. Public collision records for the most recent final year, 2025, show 129 injury collisions in the city, with 166 people hurt and one life lost. The highest counts came along Lincoln Avenue, Buena Vista Avenue, Park Street, and Central Avenue — the same routes people take to the Park Street shops, to school pickups, and to the bridges and tunnel that link Alameda to Oakland. Reported crashes here tend to peak on Tuesdays in the early hours, roughly midnight to 2 a.m.

If one of those numbers now describes you or someone in your family, the practical questions come fast: who pays the medical bills, what to say to an adjuster, whether to keep working through the pain. LawProactive exists to take one decision off your plate. We are a free service that connects injured people in Alameda with an independent personal injury attorney. We are not a law firm, we do not give legal advice, and we never charge you anything. The attorney you are connected with works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Reaching out early simply gives you more room to make good choices.

items.title: The clock in California is real
items.desc: Most injury claims must be filed within two years of the date of injury. If a public entity like a city bus or a poorly maintained public sidewalk is involved, a formal claim may be due in as little as six months.

items.title: Partial fault doesn't shut the door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning your recovery is reduced by your share of responsibility rather than wiped out. You can still pursue a claim even if you think you were partly to blame.

items.title: Pain and suffering aren't capped
items.desc: In ordinary California injury cases there is no statutory ceiling on non-economic damages such as pain, lost enjoyment of life, and emotional distress. An attorney can help you document those losses properly.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: The attorneys in our network work on contingency. You pay nothing up front, and the connection through LawProactive is completely free.

items.question: How long do I have to file an injury claim in Alameda?
items.answer: For most personal injury claims in California, the deadline is two years from the date you were hurt. That window can shrink dramatically — sometimes to six months for a required notice — when the responsible party is a city, county, transit agency, or other government entity. Because the deadline depends on who caused the harm, it is worth confirming your situation sooner rather than later.

items.question: Where do collisions cluster in Alameda?
items.answer: According to public collision records for 2025, Alameda logged 129 injury collisions, with 166 people injured and one fatality. The corridors with the highest counts were Lincoln Avenue, Buena Vista Avenue, Park Street, and Central Avenue. These are simply the streets that appear most often in the records; many of them carry a large share of the island's daily traffic.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the crash?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault. Your compensation is reduced in proportion to your percentage of responsibility, but it is not eliminated. For example, being found 20 percent at fault would generally reduce what you recover by 20 percent, not to zero.

items.question: How much does it cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorney you are connected with works on a contingency basis, so there is no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: In ordinary California injury cases, there is no cap on non-economic damages, which cover things like physical pain, anxiety, and the loss of activities you used to enjoy. Every case is different, and no one can promise a particular result. An attorney can explain how those losses are typically documented and valued.
